note:
board:// at rest — four lanes, 2/2/1/2 cards, nothing changed. The live fixture reproduces the mock's own BOARD_COLS payload (same lane order, same copy), so a row in this report is a treatment difference and not a fixture difference.

THREE THINGS TO READ PAST BEFORE FILING ANYTHING. (1) WIDTH IS NOISE: the live card is capped at max-width 820px inside a 1040px frame, so its lane track clamps to the 196px minimum while the design's full-bleed card gives each lane ~249px. (2) EVERY GROUND COLOUR CARRIES ONE SYSTEMIC DELTA: the design is measured in its own default `data-color="functional"`, which re-declares the neutral ladder in oklch (`--panel` → oklch(0.212 0.010 276)); the live app adopted the hues but not that ladder, so the same difference repeats on every anchor with a background. Re-run the design side with `?color=quiet` to hold the ladder constant and see what is left. (3) A DECORATIVE DOT INHERITS TYPE: `card.kicker-dot` paints no text, so its fontFamily/fontSize/lineHeight/letterSpacing/color rows are its parent kicker's register showing through — that register is measured properly on `card.kicker`. Read backgroundColor / boxShadow / width / height on the dot and nothing else.

Everything else on these anchors — type, colour, padding, gap, radius, border, shadow — is container-independent and load-bearing.

elements.label: card.kicker-dot
elements.note: The IDENTITY register. Live reads --surface-src from data-surface-hue="plum" on the mount wrapper and resolves oklch(0.76 0.1 288) + the 3px halo. The design side is NOT the surface's own `src`: `.sfc[data-tier="2"] .sfc-k .sd` overrides tier-2 surfaces to --violet regardless of src, so the mock paints board's dot violet (#a98be0) while its tab strip paints it plum. Worth reading twice before calling either side wrong. Ignore the typography rows on this anchor — see (3) in the state note.

elements.label: card.subtitle
elements.note: SurfaceHeader supports a subtitle; BoardRenderer never passes one, so this is expected to report ABSENT in live. Not waived — the mock's "Platform · 7 issues" line is real.

elements.label: card.link
elements.note: Same affordance, different home: the design puts it in the header rail (.sfc-r), live puts it in a row beneath the lanes. Placement is not a computed style, so read this row for the type/colour register only and the placement from the DOM outline.

elements.label: lanes
elements.note: The whole PRD-01 grid: column auto-flow, minmax(196px,1fr) tracks, gap:1px over --line (the gap IS the divider), min-height 230px, overflow-x auto with contained overscroll.

elements.label: lane.first.header
elements.note: Sticky inside its lane. position/top/margin are the pair PRD-01 calls out; `position` is not in the extractor's property set, so confirm stickiness from the source and read padding/margin/type/background here.

elements.label: lane.first.count
elements.note: margin-left:auto in both. The extractor normalizes a right-aligned auto margin to `auto-end` so the count's copy length cannot masquerade as a spacing delta.

elements.label: lane.first.card
elements.note: 8px radius, elevated ground, hairline border, 8px 9px padding, 6px gap. The first .sfk is the lane's SECOND child — the sticky header is the first.

elements.label: lane.first.card.meta
elements.note: Mono 9.5px meta row. Copy differs by design: the mock's row is one pre-composed string ("LW-208 · nova.eth"), while a spec-driven card renders LABEL + value per non-title column — so expect a text INFO row here.

elements.label: lane.single-card
elements.note: The one-card lane — catches a lane that sizes to its content instead of to the grid row.

elements.label: lane.last
elements.note: The last lane. PRD-01 warns that reproducing the 1px divider with borders puts a stray edge on the two ends; this anchor is where that shows up.

unmapped.why: BoardDiffRenderer, i.e. data-mode="diff" — a different render from the current-state view this PRD covers. The mock has no diff-rows view for board at all (its proposed state marks cards in place), so there is nothing to compare it against.

The empty board. The mock has a .sf-empty register but never renders it on the board surface, so a comparison would require authoring design markup rather than vendoring it. Renderable live at any time by passing an empty items array.
Only renders past CARD_RENDER_CAP. Measured separately in anchors/board-capped.json, against the design's one cap-line register (.sft-cap).
